messages:
incident-bot: P1 alert — potential sensitive tokens found in analytics pipeline uploads. automated log-scan matched refresh_token pattern in events from 'log-forwarder-prod'. ticket: INC-1761239 https://redwood/in/INC-1761239
oncall-anna: I'm taking primary. Paging SRE + Security to triage. Grant me view access to the stream logs.
sam_security: @oncall-anna on it. do we know if these are user refresh_tokens vs internal service tokens?
dave_sre: quick grep on shard data shows lines with \"refresh_token\":\"[A-Za-z0-9\\-_.]+\" around 13:28-13:31 UTC in kinesis shard 42. looks like the forwarder pushed raw debug logs upstream.
product-support: Seeing a burst of auth 401s hitting downstream validators ~13:35, possibly expired/revoked tokens.
oncall-anna: Immediate mitigation plan (runbook step 1):
- pause log-forwarder-prod -> analytics (pause Kinesis producer)
- block egress at security group for forwarder hosts
- rotate forwarder service account keys
- identify and revoke exposed tokens
sam_security: running token extraction + revocation now. using internal script:
```
python tools/extract_tokens.py --stream log-forwarder-prod --shard 42 > /tmp/tokens.txt
./scripts/revoke_tokens.sh /tmp/tokens.txt --reason \"log-forwarder-prod leak\"
```
I will report counts when complete.
dave_sre: applied temp SG rule (sg-0a1b2c) to deny kinesis:PutRecords from forwarder pool. confirmed no new uploads after 13:40 UTC :white_check_mark:
oncall-anna: @legal @product-support heads up — we may need a customer notice depending on number of affected users. can security pull list of unique user ids from tokens?
sam_security: extracting user ids now. preliminary: 18 unique user ids across tokens, checking scopes and last activity. will attach CSV to ticket.
ops-bot: Service account rotation: created new access key for forwarder-sa (obfuscated). Old key deactivated per runbook. rotation task id: RT-9821.
sam_security: revocation script finished — 18 tokens revoked. saved evidence to INC-1761239. commands used logged.
oncall-anna: Good. Next steps:
- confirm forwarder is sanitized and not sending raw logs
- confirm rotation propagated to all forwarder instances (config push)
- generate affected-user list and surface any high-risk/VIP accounts
- if >10 users or any enterprise/VIP, legal to review customer notice
dave_sre: I'm taking 4-hour watch. I'll monitor for re-uploads, auth anomalies, and error spikes. updating status page in 30m.
legal: please assign me the ticket. prepare a draft notice but hold until we confirm scopes and any privileged customers.
product-support: drafting notice template: https://redwood/docs/incidents/templates/customer-notice-draft (will attach once legal OK) :email:
incident-bot: INC-1761239 status updated to \"mitigated\" by oncall-anna at 13:51 UTC
dave_sre: runbook excerpt + tools used:
```
aws kinesis describe-stream --stream-name log-forwarder-prod
python tools/extract_tokens.py --shard 42 > tokens.txt
./scripts/revoke_tokens.sh tokens.txt
aws iam update-access-key --access-key-id <OLD_KEY_ID> --status Inactive --user-name forwarder-sa
```
no new sensitive uploads detected in the 30m post-block. observed auth failure count returned to baseline except for the 18 revoked tokens.
product-support: drafted customer email ready, awaiting legal signoff.
legal: reviewed draft, OK to proceed with notice for affected users. please include remediation steps and contact point.
oncall-anna: Handoff: placing @dave_sre as primary for the 4h watch. leave runbook pointer and evidence in INC-1761239.
dave_sre: taking over. will post hourly updates or earlier if anything changes.
oncall-anna: thanks team — logging postmortem stub at https://redwood/pm/INC-1761239/postmortem ; will convert to full postmortem after handoff. :handshake:
